target_customer: Operations teams in small and mid sized companies, mainly in Brazil
problem: Companies run operations on spreadsheets and legacy ERPs; Jestor offers a no-code database and workflow platform with unlimited users.
business_model: SaaS subscription with a free tier and paid plans up to R$299 per month (2021)
product_category: No-code internal tools and operations platform

founders.name: Bruno Bannach
previous_startups: Software development company run with Guilherme Pinheiro
founders.background_notes: Frustration organizing his mother's pharmacy data helped inspire the product, per Startups.com.br.

founders.name: Guilherme Pinheiro
previous_startups: Software development company run with Bruno Bannach
founders.background_notes: Stayed in Brazil during YC per Startups.com.br; not listed on the YC page.

competitors.name: Zapier
competitors.what: Integration and automation tool used as a comparison

technical_complexity.rationale: A relational no-code builder with automations and integrations is substantial engineering, though the team had prior software shop experience.

defensibility.rationale: Customers' operations built on the platform create stickiness but many no-code rivals exist.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Rivals kept growing; Jestor later added AI agents and now lists many alternatives on comparison pages.

market_need_then: Startups.com.br in August 2021 said Jestor aimed to replace spreadsheets and ERPs, was near breakeven with 10 people and had clients like Loft and Sami.

branding.name_origin: A pun on the Portuguese gestor (manager) with a J, and the English jester, the king's fool, with the customer as king.

identity.logo: Light and dark logo files; no description

branding.brand_signature: Jester metaphor: the user is the king and the software adapts

brand_strength.rationale: A sourced name story with a playful metaphor, but no evidence of community or press about the brand itself.

pivots.to: Builds custom internal systems and AI agents with engineers (current site)
pivots.why: Not stated; the current site emphasizes AI and built for you systems.

outcome_analysis: Jestor was near breakeven in 2021 on 458K raised and, per Exame via search results, later reached profit. It continues as a no-code and AI platform with a mostly Brazilian base. No large priced round was found, so it stayed capital efficient rather than venture scale; no layoffs or acquisition were reported.
notes: The 458K is the first year total reported by the press, not a single round; aggregators give conflicting seed figures ($333K in Aug 2020, $0.13M, $125K) and are not used. YC lists only Bruno Bannach; Guilherme Pinheiro is named in the Startups.com.br article. The Exame article was not opened. Pipefy and Airtable sources are undated.
